title: Quick Tip: Runtime Version and Business Central Version Are Not the Same Thing
summary: Explains that Business Central has three different version numbers: the platform/internal build, the release wave name and the app.json runtime version. Only the runtime version decides which AL features compile, and it sets the minimum platform an extension can be published to. Gives the runtime-to-wave mapping and advises setting the lowest runtime you need explicitly.
key_points: Runtime version in app.json controls which AL language features and compiler behaviors are available; the platform build and release wave name are separate numbers
An extension can only be published to environments whose runtime is the same as or newer than its own
A runtime set too low breaks newer features; set too high, it requires a platform customers may not have yet
If runtime is omitted, the compiler uses the latest major it supports, which changes as the tooling updates
Runtime 15.0, 16.0 and 17.0 map to internal versions 26.0, 27.0 and 28.0, so the offset is not constant; partners on staggered updates should target the lowest runtime that meets their needs

quotes.text: An extension publishes only to environments running the same runtime or a later one, never an earlier one.
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes the core compatibility rule that runtime version is a forward-only contract between extensions and platforms

quotes.text: Treat runtime version as a compatibility contract you actively manage, not a field VS Code fills in for you.
quotes.why_it_matters: Emphasizes that developers must consciously choose runtime based on business requirements, not rely on tooling defaults
